title: Systemic Analysis of TENS Devices to Guide Future Design Improvements
coords: x and y are percent of the page image, measured from the top left
intro: Our one-page poster summarising the literature review.

hotspots.title: Title
hotspots.note: Our University of Cincinnati poster proposes TENS design improvements.

hotspots.title: Problem statement
hotspots.note: We identify the TENS user interface as a barrier to long-term use. The central column names loose wires, electrode placement and a separate controller as design problems.

hotspots.title: Garment concept
hotspots.note: We propose integrating a TENS system into a wearable garment.

hotspots.title: Proposed electrode placement
hotspots.note: In the upper-right paragraph, we propose electrodes on the chest, upper back and trapezius. The garment image below illustrates the concept.

hotspots.title: Human and mechanical argument
hotspots.note: We intended the garment to reduce loose wires and repeated electrode placement. The poster reports no activity tests.

hotspots.title: Biological and electrical argument
hotspots.note: We propose fixed electrode positions for more consistent placement. The poster reports no tests of placement or tolerance.

hotspots.title: Chemical argument
hotspots.note: We propose textile or dry electrodes to replace disposable hydrogel pads. The poster reports no measurements of skin tolerance or durability.

hotspots.title: The systems diagram
hotspots.note: The same interaction diagram as in the review, shrunk to fit the poster. The full-size version is on page 6 of the review.
